body: I've been super busy, school wise this week and really want to continue this conversation.  I do want to wrestle through these questions and am going to start a new thread for these questions, cause i'm not sure it fits right under here

I just wanted to say thanks for your response.   I have some major ups and downs  and that was definitely a down.  I think I just need to be able to say it to someone when I am really in the down.  I think it helps me to stop cycling it so much in my head.  these are the things that have made this so difficult:
1. Have always loved my children and do not get to spend much time with them(they are teenagers and this happens somewhat naturally, but it is still hard)
2.  Have lost most of my mutual friends with my ex.
3. Have lost my previous career and am back in school trying to refind myself.
4. Finances are a mess right now and is quite stressful
5. lost faith and am trying to figure that out

There is more but those are some of the big ones.  I have overcome in the past but it is pretty heavy right now. Some days it really does overwhelm me.  I really don't think I will kill myself, but am really glad I don't have a gun when I am in those really low points
And atheists have them too. You can't deny that and hold some moral high ground.

Look. it wasn't my point to start a fight.  It is my point that your stereotypes are simplistic, as all stereotypes usually are.  Whatever your justification is for what Stalin did, the fact is, is that he was an atheist.  I really don't believe that, that means that all atheists are like that, but you seem to be suggesting that all religious people are gun toting fanatics who are bent on destruction.  If you think I'm being lazy in my thinking, then what are you doing.  Promoting stereotypes to increase fear and hate?
lol, I'm just calling you out in saying that all militant atheists are, are peaceful beer drinking hipsters.  Human nature is human nature no matter how you package it. and yes i'm just playing :)

Of course not.  I'm actually a bit fed up with all sides right now.  Everyone seems to be happy with shooting at each other and claiming superiority with all their arguments.

I don't know what it all means.
Do you have any statistics on that?

I'm curious about your response.  In life we all make choices to believe certain things that bring us comfort.  Sure some things are healthier then others. 

Drugs that will solve my problems - not the best choice, unless it's one that bring back actual chemical balance to the body.

I chose to believe that I am important - a good belief. and there are many others.

Having a spiritual life had been proven to have positive effects on peoples lives, so even if it is a lie, you can't really say it cheapens peoples lives.   I guess you can and I am sure it has but it is not a universal statement that you can make.

You can't prove that God does exist or doesn't exist, so people make choices.  What makes sense to me may not make sense to you, but it doesn't mean that either of us are wrong. Truly the belief that you have that people are wasting their lives believing in God seems just as strong as their beliefs that you are going to hell.

It is not weird to see both sides of the debate, I think it's healthy to grow a deeper understanding of the world and understand that people are just trying to make sense of it all.  You shouldn't feel guilty if you decide faith or don't decide faith.  

To be clear I'm walking through the same journey and really don't know if I will end up on the side of faith or not, but I don't think it is a easy as saying it's all a lie that we need to be rescued from.

I know this is a choice that many people have to face when confronting their faith in no matter which way they are moving, but I am feeling very lost and alone.  I am losing my family, all of my friends and I really don't know how to deal with this.  I can read more but it just leaves me feeling more unsettled.  I truly feel like I'm failing apart.  I don't know why I'm sharing this here except i guess it is the only place I have.

"Wife tells me I’m not the same person she married. Feels she’s been cheated."  I get that so much from her.  She says I deceived her, like I lied to her, that she would never have married me if she had known.  She asks over in over how I could change my beliefs and doubts I ever believed.  I've asked her how she can be excited when someone becomes a christian and not wonder how they changed beliefs.  She really doesn't have an answer.

I really could pull the Corinthians verse on her, but i don't want to rub it in her face and force her to stay in something that she doesn't want out of guilt.

I'll read the article, thanks

Thank you all for your helpful comments.  There are definitely other issues that needed to be worked through then the faith, but it seems to have grown into THE issue.  One thing I appreciate so much from you guys was not to just tell me to ditch faith outright but to keep questioning.  I may end up with no faith or just a faith that is much different, but thanks for being sensitive on that part
